sources.title: o1 API model reference
sources.evidence: Exact o1 alias points to o1-2024-12-17 and is marked shut down. Last-documented specifications are 200,000 context, 100,000 output, text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling. Exact cached-input pricing establishes o1 caching support. No parameter count is given.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT Pro — December 5, 2024
sources.evidence: Dated first-party announcement offers full OpenAI o1 in ChatGPT on December 5. It separately describes o1 pro mode; this report audits ordinary o1, not the preview or pro mode.

sources.title: OpenAI o1 and new tools for developers
sources.evidence: Explicitly calls o1-2024-12-17 a new post-trained version of the model released in ChatGPT two weeks earlier. Documents function calling, structured outputs, developer messages, vision and reasoning-effort control. API rollout initially targets usage tier 5.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: December 17, 2024 entry releases full o1 in the API with function calling, developer messages, structured outputs, vision and reasoning-effort control. The September release instead names o1-preview and o1-mini; neither replaces the December 5 full-o1 public release date.

sources.title: OpenAI o1 System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded the full 52-page PDF and inspected training, testing scope and exact o1 evaluations. Distinguishes near-final and December 5 checkpoints. Footnote explicitly says the card predates the December 17 update. It discloses reinforcement learning and training-data categories but no production total/active count or detailed topology.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-4.5 System Card — February 27, 2025
sources.evidence: Downloaded full later report and inspected exact o1 columns in text/image refusal, jailbreak, hallucination and related evaluations. These are performance scores, not size or topology disclosures. Searched the full text for parameter and architecture disclosures; no exact o1 count found.

sources.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded full later first-party report. Figure 4 compares HealthBench performance with exact o1 and qualitatively calls gpt-oss-20b smaller. Its parameter table describes the released gpt-oss checkpoints, not o1. No numerical o1 total or active count is supplied.

sources.title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
sources.evidence: Read full-text training-method sections and exact o1 comparison table. Section 2.4 says the RL reward signal was added for o1 and o3-mini; reported counts and metrics do not specify production o1 parameters or architecture. SFT/RL methodology is not an architecture count.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived recipe explicitly scopes itself to models before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI prompt caching as reuse of key/value projections in Transformer attention layers. Combined with exact o1 cached-input pricing and its 2024 release, this supports only a qualified broad Transformer inference, not dense/MoE structure or a size.

sources.title: Learning Powerful Models: From Transformers to Reasoners and Beyond
sources.evidence: Read the public OpenAI research presentation transcript. It discusses Transformer priors and reasoning models and compares o1 results, but says reasoning models are usually Transformers rather than specifying an exact o1 topology. Its hypothetical scaling counts are not o1 production parameters.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: For vision-capable models, PDF inputs are processed into extracted text and page images. This supports PDF as a documented API input format alongside native text/image input; it is not an independent neural modality or evidence of a live retired endpoint.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: April 22, 2026 announcement explicitly identifies o1 and o1-2024-12-17; access shut down October 23, 2026. Specifications are preserved as last-documented capabilities, with no claim that requests still succeed.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 provide limited API/service-use rights and reserve service intellectual property. Together with the hosted product/API release, this supports a descriptive Proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: All OpenAI models
sources.evidence: Official catalog identifies o1 as a shut-down reasoning model and separately lists the Apache-licensed gpt-oss open-weight models. No o1 checkpoint distribution is listed.

sources.title: EU AI Act: OpenAI Resources and Customer Guidance
sources.evidence: Checked the published training-summary index; it has no exact o1 summary. Summaries for newer GPT models were not transferred to o1.

sources.title: Models.dev o1 record
sources.evidence: Read the upstream lead independently. It provides the December 5 release, broad o-family label, context and capability flags, but no parameter evidence. Primary releases and technical sources were used for verification.

sources.title: Attempted later o3-mini system card
sources.evidence: Direct web fetch returned 404. This unavailable document is not used to establish any field; accessible later GPT-4.5 and gpt-oss reports were inspected instead.

name.note: Exact ordinary full-model name; distinguish o1-preview, o1-mini and o1 pro mode.

family.note: The exact reference and system card explicitly identify the o1 model family; use this more specific family within the broader o-series.

release_date.note: Earliest public full-o1 release in ChatGPT. The December 17 API snapshot is a later post-trained revision; September o1-preview is a different model.

open_weights.note: Released through proprietary hosted products and API; no public o1 weight distribution is documented. Open-weight gpt-oss is explicitly separate.

license.note: Descriptive licensing classification based on limited hosted-service rights; not an SPDX weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total production parameter count found in the original card, exact o1 columns of later first-party reports or checked training/research sources. Relative size comparisons and hypothetical scaling figures do not establish a numeric o1 total.

active_parameters_b.note: No active parameter count or expert-routing specification found. Do not equate undisclosed total and active counts or import gpt-oss counts.

architecture.note: Qualified broad inference: exact o1 cached-input pricing binds it to prompt caching, and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering recipe describes Transformer attention and KV reuse. This is not an exact o1 architecture specification; layer count, dense versus MoE structure and multimodal component topology remain undisclosed. Training research and the general reasoning-model talk do not justify more detail.

context_window.note: Last-documented API context for default o1-2024-12-17; maximum output is separately 100,000 tokens. This is not a claim that the original December 5 ChatGPT product exposed the same context or that the retired API still operates.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API file format converted to text and page images. No native audio/video support is claimed; API capabilities are last documented after shutdown.

reasoning.note: Explicit reinforcement-learning-based reasoning and internal chain of thought; API revision supports configurable reasoning effort.

tool_call.note: Function calling explicitly introduced for the December 17 API revision and retained in the last-documented reference. Do not retroactively attribute all API tools to December 5 ChatGPT or claim a currently live endpoint.

description.value: Reasoning model for complex tasks with text and image input and support for function calling.
description.note: Plain description of documented capabilities; release/revision and retirement qualifications are kept in notes.

patch.description: Reasoning model for complex tasks with text and image input and support for function calling.

sources.label: OpenAI o1 and new tools for developers

patch.notes: Full o1 first released in ChatGPT on December 5, 2024. The API default o1-2024-12-17 is a later post-trained revision with function calling and vision; its last-documented context is 200,000 tokens with 100,000 maximum output. OpenAI shut down o1 and that API snapshot on October 23, 2026. PDF input is converted to text and page images. Broad Transformer architecture is inferred from exact-model caching support and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering explanation; detailed topology, total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed.

summary: Confirm December 5 full-o1 public release while distinguishing December 17 API post-training revision and October 23, 2026 shutdown. Add specific o1 family, Proprietary classification, plain description and qualified broad Transformer inference. Counts remain undisclosed after original, later exact-model table and training/research checks; last-documented context and capabilities are retained with explicit scope.
